stem: A platform team calls a module straight from GitHub with `source = "github.com/acme/queue-module"`. A colleague merged an unfinished change into the repository's primary branch, and the next fresh workspace picked it up during initialization. The team wants every new workspace to receive the code of the release tagged v2.3.0. What should they change?

choices.text: Rewrite the address in the explicit `git::https://github.com/acme/queue-module.git` form

rationale: The `ref` query parameter accepts a tag name, so naming the release tag fixes which revision is cloned. A double slash marks a folder inside the package, not a revision, so `//v2.3.0` would be read as a folder named v2.3.0 inside the repository, which does not exist, instead of selecting the tag. A branch name is accepted by `ref` as well, but a branch keeps moving as commits arrive, so it does not fix a version. The explicit `git::` form of the same repository still follows the default branch at HEAD when no `ref` is given.
